assignments.note: 2024-03 The misleading success of simulating social interactions with LLMs
assignments.why: Measures how faithful LLM simulation of interaction partners is (omniscient vs non-omniscient), showing simulation-based evaluation of social agents overestimates ability.

assignments.note: 2024-04 Autonomous Evaluation and Refinement of Digital Agents
assignments.why: VLM/LLM judges that read web and device-control trajectories (judge design), scored against oracle metrics of agent benchmarks like WebArena.

assignments.note: 2024-04 LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
assignments.why: Empirical measurement of judge self-preference bias and its causal link to self-recognition; the subject is the judge.
A regression method that removes length bias from an automatic LLM evaluator, a method to make the judge less biased.
369-task desktop agent benchmark whose scoring is execution-based verification of final machine state by per-task checker scripts.
A judge design using a panel of diverse LLM judges whose scores are aggregated by max/average voting instead of a single judge.
Aligns LLM and code assertion judges to user grades (judge design) and frames validating the judge against humans, a judge-the-judge loop.
Evaluator agent with memory that iteratively refines generated misconduct scenarios against the target, with a tool-using evaluator judging responses.
LLM peer battles in an arena judged by a committee of LLM judges that discusses and votes, aggregating several judges' verdicts.
Measures LLM evaluator biases on SummEval (familiarity, skew, low agreement), with prompt sensitivity and cross-attribute anchoring as core findings.
Foundation models generate an open-ended stream of new agent environments as code with success detectors, i.e. generated task suites for agents.
Fine-tuned open evaluator LMs for direct and pairwise assessment built by weight merging; the subject is the judge.
Agent environment of user tasks and prompt-injection test cases scored by deterministic environment-state checks.
LLM-judged pairwise benchmark built to reproduce Arena rankings, i.e. arena-style pairwise evaluation automated with a judge.
Examiner/Questioner/Assessor agents iteratively generate harder targeted test questions from discovered weaknesses, with an LLM Assessor grading.
Benchmark scored by evaluator LMs with instance-specific rubrics, a judge-prompting method to fix vague criteria.

assignments.note: 2024-06 CriticGPT LLM Critics Help Catch LLM Bugs
assignments.why: RLHF-trained code critic whose reward model is learned from human pairwise critique comparisons; the subject is the critic as judge.
Measures judge alignment with human labels on TriviaQA (kappa vs agreement, leniency, sensitivity to dummy answers); measurement is the contribution.

assignments.note: 2024-06 LLMs instead of human judges JUDGE-BENCH
assignments.why: Large meta-evaluation of LLM judges against human annotations across 20 datasets.
A council of 20 LLMs judges one another and their judgments are aggregated democratically into rankings, a multi-judge alternative to a single judge.
A test set that is continually refreshed and replaced from new sources to stay ahead of contamination, scored by ground truth rather than judges.

assignments.note: 2024-06 Scaling Laws for RM Overoptimization in Direct Alignment
assignments.why: Studies overoptimization of the implicit reward in DPO/IPO-style preference learning, showing reward-model-like hump curves.
150K-judgment audit of position bias in pairwise/listwise LLM judges, i.e. verdicts changing with option order.
Tool-agent benchmark graded by final DB state with pass^k, where the user is an LLM simulator with a hidden scenario.
Critique of agent benchmark practice: accuracy-only reporting, cost, missing holdouts, reproducibility.
An LM iteratively proposes and refines benchmark descriptions and generates Q/A sets optimised to expose model weaknesses.
An autorater fine-tuned on 100+ quality-assessment tasks and 5M+ human judgments.
A meta-judge creates pairwise preference data to DPO-train the model's own judge role, a self-improving judge loop.

assignments.note: 2024-07 On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs
assignments.why: Compares debate and consultancy against direct QA as protocols in which weaker LLM judges evaluate stronger agents.

assignments.note: 2024-07 Prover-verifier games improve legibility of LLM outputs
assignments.why: A prover-verifier game (verifier commits, helpful and sneaky provers best-respond) that trains small verifiers to check strong-model solutions.
